label: A
steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand.
Fold all fingers tightly over your palm.
Hold your thumb resting against the side of your index finger.
Keep the fist upright facing forward.
tip: Keep fingers firmly closed — do not let the thumb stick up.

label: B
steps: Extend all four fingers straight up, held together.
Bend your thumb flat across your palm.
Hold the hand upright with palm facing forward.
tip: Fingers must be straight and touching each other.

label: C
steps: Curve all fingers and thumb to form a 'C' shape.
Face the opening of the C to the side.
Fingers and thumb should be parallel and curved.
tip: Imagine holding a small cylinder — that is the C shape.

label: D
steps: Extend your index finger straight up.
Touch the tips of your middle, ring, and pinky fingers to your thumb tip.
Face the hand forward with index finger pointing up.
tip: The circle formed by thumb and fingers is the round part of 'D'.

label: E
steps: Bend all four fingers down so their tips touch the upper palm.
Fold your thumb inward under the bent fingers.
Hold the hand with knuckles facing outward.
tip: The bent fingers resemble the horizontal lines of the letter E.

label: F
steps: Touch the tip of your index finger to the tip of your thumb, forming a circle.
Extend your other three fingers straight out and slightly spread.
Hold the hand upright facing forward.
tip: Similar to the OK sign but with three fingers spread wide.

label: G
steps: Extend your index finger pointing to the side (horizontally).
Extend your thumb pointing in the same direction.
Curl remaining fingers into the palm.
Hold hand sideways with thumb and index parallel.
tip: Think of a gun pointing sideways — that is G.

label: H
steps: Extend your index and middle finger together, pointing to the side.
Keep the two fingers side-by-side horizontally.
Curl ring, pinky, and thumb into the palm.
tip: The two horizontal fingers represent the two strokes of 'H'.

label: I
steps: Extend only your pinky finger straight up.
Curl all other fingers into a fist.
Keep the pinky pointing upward.
tip: Only the smallest finger — the I finger — stands up.

label: J
steps: Start with the pinky extended (like I).
Trace the shape of the letter J in the air with your pinky.
Move down, then curve left (or right for left-handers).
tip: J is a movement sign — trace the shape smoothly in the air.

label: K
steps: Extend your index finger pointing upward.
Extend your middle finger diagonally outward.
Place your thumb between the index and middle finger.
Curl ring and pinky into the palm.
tip: The spread index and middle fingers look like the two diagonal strokes of K.

label: L
steps: Extend your index finger pointing straight up.
Extend your thumb pointing horizontally to the side.
Curl remaining fingers into the palm.
The hand forms an L shape.
tip: Very intuitive — your hand literally makes the letter L.

label: M
steps: Make a fist with the thumb tucked inside.
Drape three fingers (index, middle, ring) over the thumb.
Keep pinky folded in.
tip: Three fingers over the thumb — three humps of M.

label: N
steps: Tuck thumb inside a fist.
Drape only index and middle finger over the thumb.
Keep ring and pinky folded in.
tip: Two fingers — two humps of N.

label: O
steps: Curve all fingers and bring their tips to meet the thumb tip.
Form a rounded O shape.
Hold the hand so the O faces forward.
tip: Make a circle with all your fingers touching the thumb.

label: P
steps: Extend index finger pointing downward.
Extend middle finger pointing outward/diagonal.
Place thumb between index and middle.
Face the hand downward (rotated K).
tip: P is K rotated so the index finger points down.

label: Q
steps: Extend index finger pointing downward.
Extend thumb pointing downward alongside it.
Curl remaining fingers into the palm.
Hold with both extended fingers pointing down.
tip: G rotated downward — both index and thumb point down.

label: R
steps: Extend your index and middle finger.
Cross the middle finger over the index finger.
Keep ring and pinky curled. Thumb folded.
Hold crossed fingers upright.
tip: Crossed fingers — like crossing your fingers for luck — is R.

label: S
steps: Make a fist.
Wrap fingers over the thumb so the thumb is visible at the side.
Keep the fist tight with knuckles facing out.
tip: A tight fist with thumb wrapped by fingers, not inside.

label: T
steps: Make a fist.
Place your thumb between your index and middle finger tips.
The thumb tip should poke out between those fingers.
tip: Thumb tip pokes between index and middle finger.

label: U
steps: Extend your index and middle fingers together, pointing upward.
Keep the two fingers side-by-side and straight.
Curl thumb, ring, and pinky into the palm.
tip: Two straight fingers together pointing up — like the sides of U.

label: V
steps: Extend your index and middle fingers in a V shape (spread apart).
Point both fingers upward.
Curl remaining fingers and thumb into the palm.
tip: The classic victory/peace sign — V for victory.

label: W
steps: Extend index, middle, and ring fingers spread apart upward.
Keep thumb and pinky folded.
Three spread fingers form the three points of W.
tip: Three spread fingers like a trident — W shape.

label: X
steps: Extend your index finger.
Bend/hook it at the middle joint so it curves.
Curl remaining fingers and thumb into the palm.
tip: A hooked index finger that looks like a bent X.

label: Y
steps: Extend your thumb pointing to the side.
Extend your pinky pointing upward.
Curl index, middle, and ring fingers into the palm.
tip: Thumb and pinky extended — the classic 'hang loose' / call-me gesture.

label: Z
steps: Extend your index finger.
Trace a Z shape in the air: move right, diagonally down-left, then right again.
Keep remaining fingers curled.
tip: Z is a movement sign — trace the zigzag shape of the letter.

steps: Extend only your index finger pointing straight up.
Curl all other fingers and your thumb into the palm.
tip: One finger = one.

steps: Extend your index and middle fingers upward, spread apart in a V shape.
Curl thumb, ring, and pinky into the palm.
tip: Two fingers spread = two.

steps: Extend thumb, index, and middle fingers.
Keep ring and pinky curled into the palm.
Spread the three extended fingers slightly.
tip: Three fingers out — easy to remember.

steps: Extend all four fingers (index, middle, ring, pinky) upward.
Curl thumb into the palm.
Keep four fingers straight and together.
tip: Four fingers up, thumb hidden.

steps: Spread all five fingers wide open, palm facing forward.
Keep all fingers and thumb extended.
tip: Open palm with all fingers spread = five.

steps: Extend thumb and pinky, curl index, middle, and ring fingers.
This is the same as Y/hang-loose for 6 in ISL number system.
Some regional variants: tap pinky to thumb.
tip: Thumb and pinky out — the 6 handshape.

steps: Extend index and pinky fingers upward (like rock-on sign).
Curl middle and ring fingers into the palm.
Thumb may be extended or curled depending on regional variation.
tip: Rock-on sign with thumb tucked = 7.

steps: Extend middle finger and thumb, touch their tips together.
Keep index slightly extended or bent; ring and pinky curled.
Some regions: open F-hand with middle finger flicking down.
tip: Middle finger and thumb touching = 8.

steps: Touch index finger tip to thumb tip to form a circle.
Extend middle, ring, and pinky fingers upward.
This is similar to the F-handshape used for 9.
tip: Circle of index+thumb = 9.

steps: Make a fist (0 or A shape) with the dominant hand.
Shake or wiggle the hand/thumb to indicate 'ten'.
Some variants: show 1 then 0 in sequence.
tip: A shake of the fist or sequential 1-0 represents 10.

label: Namaste
steps: Bring both palms together in front of your chest.
Keep fingers pointing upward, thumbs close to the chest.
Slight bow of the head is optional but adds warmth.
tip: The universal Indian greeting — palms together at chest level.

label: Hello
steps: Open your dominant hand flat, palm facing outward.
Hold the hand at shoulder or head height.
Wave side to side gently 2–3 times.
tip: A friendly open-palm wave at shoulder height.

label: Thank You
steps: Bring your dominant hand flat, fingers together.
Touch the fingertips to your chin.
Move the hand forward and slightly downward away from the chin.
tip: The hand moves from chin outward — gratitude flowing outward.

label: Good Morning
steps: Hold both hands at chest level, palms up.
Move both hands upward and outward to shoulder level.
Open them like a sunrise.
tip: Imagine the sun rising — hands lift and open outward.

label: Good Night
steps: Cup your dominant hand over your non-dominant fist.
Bring both hands down from eye level to chest level.
Close your eyes briefly (optional) to convey night.
tip: Hands come down like night descending.

label: Welcome
steps: Extend both arms forward, palms up.
Sweep both hands inward toward your body in a welcoming gesture.
tip: Arms open outward then sweep in — welcoming someone in.

label: Goodbye
steps: Open your dominant hand wide, palm facing the other person.
Wave it side to side 2–3 times at shoulder height.
Alternatively, move the hand away from the body while waving.
tip: Similar to Hello wave, but slightly more final — the hand often moves away.

label: Nice to meet you
steps: Extend both hands forward, palms facing each other.
Bring them together once in a gentle handshake motion.
Nod head slightly while doing this.
tip: A brief two-hand clasp or handshake motion with a nod.

label: Love
steps: Extend thumb, index finger, and pinky.
Curl middle and ring fingers into the palm.
Hold the hand up — this is also the ASL 'I love you' hand.
In ISL: you may also cross both hands over the chest.
tip: Thumb, index, and pinky extended — a universally recognised love sign.

label: Yes
steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand.
Nod the fist up and down at wrist level, mimicking a head nod.
tip: The fist nods 'yes' just like your head would.

label: No
steps: Extend your index and middle fingers together.
Tap them against your extended thumb, opening and closing quickly.
This creates a snapping motion.
tip: Index and middle finger snap against thumb — like a quick 'no no no'.

label: Please
steps: Place your dominant hand flat on your chest, palm inward.
Move the hand in a circular motion on your chest (clockwise).
tip: A circular rub on the chest — humble and sincere.

label: Sorry
steps: Make a fist with your dominant hand.
Place it on your chest.
Rub it in a circular motion on your chest.
tip: A fist rubbing the chest — feeling of regret over the heart.

label: Home
steps: Bring fingertips together above palm to make a rooftop shape.
Both hands can form the roof peak with touching fingertips.
Then sweep hands apart and downward for the walls (optional).
tip: Fingertips touching above form the roof of a house.

label: Food / Eat
steps: Bring all fingertips of dominant hand together.
Bring the pinched fingers to your mouth repeatedly.
This mimics eating food.
tip: Fingers pinched together move to the mouth — universal eating gesture.

label: Water
steps: Extend your index, middle, and ring fingers.
Tap your index finger to your chin twice.
Some variations: make a W handshape and tap chin.
tip: Tapping the chin with two or three fingers means water.

label: Toilet
steps: Make a T handshape (thumb between index and middle fingers).
Shake the hand slightly side to side.
tip: T handshape shaken = toilet. A very useful sign in daily life.

label: Doctor
steps: Place the fingertips of your dominant hand on the inside wrist of your other hand.
Mimic checking a pulse.
tip: Two fingers on the wrist — feeling for a pulse = doctor.

label: Family
steps: Make an F handshape with both hands (index to thumb).
Place them together in front, thumbs touching.
Rotate both hands outward in a circle until pinkies touch.
tip: Both F-hands circle outward — the family circle.

label: School
steps: Hold non-dominant hand palm up.
Clap dominant hand down onto it twice.
tip: Two claps on the open palm — teacher clapping for attention in class.

label: Book
steps: Hold both hands together, palms touching (closed book).
Open them outward like opening a book.
tip: Hands open like a book — simple and visual.

label: Pain / Hurt
steps: Extend both index fingers.
Point them toward each other and twist them in opposite directions near the painful body part.
tip: Two index fingers twisting toward each other — the twisting shows pain.

label: Happy
steps: Place your dominant hand flat on your chest, palm inward.
Brush it upward twice in a quick, light motion.
tip: Happiness rising from the heart upward.

label: Sad
steps: Hold both hands open with fingertips pointing toward your face.
Draw both hands downward along your cheeks (like tears falling).
tip: Hands mimicking tears streaming down the cheeks.

label: Help
steps: Place your dominant hand in an A-shape (fist, thumb up) on your non-dominant flat palm.
Lift both hands upward together.
tip: One fist lifted by the flat palm — being lifted up = help.

label: Go
steps: Extend both index fingers pointing forward.
Move both hands forward away from the body.
tip: Both index fingers point and move in the direction of travel.

label: Stop
steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat, palm up.
Bring the edge of your dominant hand down sharply onto the non-dominant palm.
tip: A sharp karate-chop onto the open palm = stop.

label: What
steps: Extend all fingers, palm facing up.
Shake the hand side to side with a questioning expression.
tip: Open palm shaking side to side with a quizzical look = what?
